knowledge_point.title: Identifying True Statements Using the Invertible Matrix Theorem and the Rank-Nullity Theorem

question.:question/problem:
Which of the following statements are true, given that $A$ is a $4\times 4$ matrix and 

$$
\text{Null}(A)=\text{Span}\left\{\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ -2 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}\right\}?
$$

Select all that apply.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $A$ is a $4\times 4$ matrix, the invertible matrix theorem states the following:

$A$ is invertible

$$
\Longleftrightarrow\quad\left\{\begin{aligned}\operatorname{Col}(A) &=\mathbb{R}^{4} \\ \dim(\operatorname{Col}(A)) &=4=\operatorname{rank}(A) \\ \operatorname{Null}(A) &=\{0\} \\ \dim(\operatorname{Null}(A)) &=0=\operatorname{nullity}(A)\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Also, according to the rank-nullity theorem, if $A$ is a matrix with $n$ columns, then 

$$
\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A)=n.
$$

The supplied null space has the independent spanning vectors

$$
\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ -2 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}
$$

Thus $\text{nullity}(A)=1.$

By the rank-nullity theorem,

$$
\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A)=n.
$$

$$
\text{rank}(A)+1=4,\qquad \text{rank}(A)=4-1=3.
$$

Hence $\text{rank}(A)=3$ and $\text{nullity}(A)=1$. Since rank is less than the number of columns, $A$ is not invertible and $\det(A)=0$. Also, $\text{Col}(A)$ has dimension 3. The number of pivot columns is 3, and the number of non-pivot columns is 1.

- Statement “$\text{Col}(A)={R}^{4}$” is false. The column-space dimension is 3, less than 4.

- Statement “$\text{rank}(A)=4$” is false. $\text{rank}(A)=3$.

- Statement “The number of non-pivot columns in $A$ is equal to $1$” is true. The number of non-pivot columns is 1.

Therefore, the correct answer is The number of non-pivot columns in $A$ is equal to $1$.

:question/answer-fields.:answer-field/key: The number of non-pivot columns in $A$ is equal to $1$

question.:question/problem:
Which of the following statements are true, given that $A$ is a $5\times 5$ matrix and 

$$
\text{Null}(A)=\text{Span}\left\{\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\,\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 0 \\ -3 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}\right\}?
$$

Select all that apply.
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $A$ is a $5\times 5$ matrix, the invertible matrix theorem states the following:

$A$ is invertible

$$
\Longleftrightarrow\quad\left\{\begin{aligned}\operatorname{Col}(A) &=\mathbb{R}^{5} \\ \dim(\operatorname{Col}(A)) &=5=\operatorname{rank}(A) \\ \operatorname{Null}(A) &=\{0\} \\ \dim(\operatorname{Null}(A)) &=0=\operatorname{nullity}(A)\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Also, according to the rank-nullity theorem, if $A$ is a matrix with $n$ columns, then 

$$
\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A)=n.
$$

The supplied null space has the independent spanning vectors

$$
\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ -2 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\;\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 0 \\ -3 \\ 0 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}
$$

Thus $\text{nullity}(A)=2.$

By the rank-nullity theorem,

$$
\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A)=n.
$$

$$
\text{rank}(A)+2=5,\qquad \text{rank}(A)=5-2=3.
$$

Hence $\text{rank}(A)=3$ and $\text{nullity}(A)=2$. Since rank is less than the number of columns, $A$ is not invertible and $\det(A)=0$. Also, $\text{Col}(A)$ has dimension 3. The number of pivot columns is 3, and the number of non-pivot columns is 2.

- Statement “$A$ is not invertible” is true. The rank is less than the number of columns.

- Statement “$\text{Col}(A)\ne {R}^{5}$” is true. The column-space dimension is 3, less than 5.

- Statement “$\text{rank}(A)=3$” is true. $\text{rank}(A)=3$.

Therefore, the correct answer is $A$ is not invertible; $\text{Col}(A)\ne {R}^{5}$; $\text{rank}(A)=3$.

Also, according to the rank-nullity theorem, if $A$ is a matrix with $n$ columns, then 

$$
\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A)=n.
$$

The supplied null space has the independent spanning vectors

$$
\begin{bmatrix}5 \\ -4 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix},\;\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 0 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{bmatrix}
$$

Thus $\text{nullity}(A)=2.$

By the rank-nullity theorem,

$$
\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A)=n.
$$

$$
\text{rank}(A)+2=4,\qquad \text{rank}(A)=4-2=2.
$$

question.:question/problem:
Which of the following statements are true, given that $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix and  $\text{Null}(A)=\{\begin{bmatrix}3{x}_{1} \\ 4{x}_{1} \\ -5{x}_{1}\end{bmatrix}\,|\,{x}_{1}\in R\}?$ 

I. $\text{rank}(A)=2$

II. $A$ is not invertible

III. $det(A)\ne 0$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Since $A$ is a $3\times 3$ matrix, the invertible matrix theorem states the following:

$A$ is invertible

$\,⇔\,\{\,\begin{aligned} & \text{Col}(A)={R}^{3} \\  & \text{dim(Col}(A))=3=\text{rank}(A) \\  & \text{Null}(A)=\{0\} \\  & \text{dim(Null}(A))=0=\text{nullity}(A)\end{aligned}$  

Also, according to the rank-nullity theorem, if $A$ is a matrix with $n$ columns, then 

$$
\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A)=n.
$$

The supplied null space has the independent spanning vectors

$$
\begin{bmatrix}3 \\ 4 \\ -5\end{bmatrix}
$$

Thus $\text{nullity}(A)=1.$

By the rank-nullity theorem,

$$
\text{rank}(A)+\text{nullity}(A)=n.
$$

$$
\text{rank}(A)+1=3,\qquad \text{rank}(A)=3-1=2.
$$

Hence $\text{rank}(A)=2$ and $\text{nullity}(A)=1$. Since rank is less than the number of columns, $A$ is not invertible and $\det(A)=0$. Also, $\text{Col}(A)$ has dimension 2. The number of pivot columns is 2, and the number of non-pivot columns is 1.

- Statement I is true. $\text{rank}(A)=2$.

- Statement II is true. The rank is less than the number of columns.

- Statement III is false. $A$ is not invertible, so $\det(A)=0$.

Therefore, the correct answer is I and II only.
